brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Half bases stacked at levels 0, 1 and 2 in the same cell (piece:0,0,0, 0,0,1 and 0,0,2), joined by snaps.
drawer:0#0,0#cut sits on the cut face of the bottom half base. Only one drawer fits in a half-base storey.

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,2~hex-bin-half-n-full-div2, a two-compartment bin on level 2 with no top cover, so it stays open.

finish.summary: I built a single tower three storeys tall. It's made of north half bases rather than full ones, because a drawer only seats on the cut face of a half base, and the configurator only allows the same kind of base on top of another. The bottom storey has a drawer. The middle storey is empty: you didn't ask for anything there, and solid caps close it. The top storey holds an open bin split into two compartments, with no cover over it. The open sides of the bottom and middle storeys and one edge of the top are capped. I didn't add joint bolts because the configurator said they would change nothing. The build check passed with no errors and no collisions between parts. One limit: a half-base tower is half the footprint of a full one, so there is one half-size drawer and one half-size bin.

M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
